accessRequest.An administrator reviews the request. On: An administrator reviews the request. Once approved, the assets show up in your asset list until the end time
accessRequest.The permission of this request is delete: The permission of this request is deleted and its connected sessions are disconnected
accessRequest.The request has been sent to the adminis: The request has been sent to the administrators

account.A login rule requires two-step verificat: A login rule requires two-step verification for your account. Turn it on to go on using Casvisor
account.Ask for a code from an authenticator app: Ask for a code from an authenticator app such as Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or 1Password after the password
account.Auto rotate - Tooltip: Casvisor changes the password on the asset to a new random one on schedule, through the asset's own account, which must be root, able to sudo without a password, or a Windows administrator. Only accounts with a password and no private key are rotated
account.Casvisor creates this account on the ass: Casvisor creates this account on the asset if it does not exist and sets the saved password there
account.Casvisor sets a new random password for: Casvisor sets a new random password for this account on the asset and keeps it. Connected sessions are not affected
account.Scan the QR code with the authenticator: Scan the QR code with the authenticator app, or enter this key
account.Successfully signed out, redirected to h: Successfully signed out, redirected to homepage
account.The account is set on the asset: The account is set on the asset
account.The two passwords do not match: The two passwords do not match
account.Then enter the 6-digit code it shows: Then enter the 6-digit code it shows
account.Users connect as these accounts without: Users connect as these accounts without seeing their passwords. The asset's own account above is the default account, and Casvisor uses it to change the passwords of the others

accountBackup.Include assets - Tooltip: Also put the assets in the backup, with the passwords and private keys of their own accounts, as assets.csv in the format of the asset import. Without them, a lost Casvisor can't be rebuilt from the backup
accountBackup.No webhook of the Email type yet: No webhook of the Email type yet, add one on
accountBackup.Overwrite - Tooltip: Off: only the assets and accounts that are missing are added, and the ones that exist are left as they are. On: the existing ones are also set back to the backup, passwords included, which undoes the password changes made since the backup
accountBackup.Overwrite the assets and accounts that a: Overwrite the assets and accounts that already exist
accountBackup.Password - Tooltip: The password the zip file is encrypted with, at least 12 characters. Keep it apart from the backup: whoever has both can read every password
accountBackup.Restore - Description: The zip file of a backup of this or another Casvisor and its password. The assets come back first, then their accounts. Preview it first to see what would change
accountBackup.Schedule - Tooltip: A cron line such as 0 2 * * 0 for 02:00 every Sunday, when the backup is made and emailed. Empty: only by hand
accountBackup.Send with - Tooltip: The webhooks of the Email type the backup is sent with, as an attachment

accountRisk.Lock - Description: Each account is locked on its asset and expired, so that it can sign in neither with a password nor with a key; on Windows it is disabled. Undo it on the asset with usermod -U -e -1, or Enable-LocalUser
accountRisk.Manage - Description: Each account becomes a system account of its asset, with a random password set on the asset and rotated every 30 days. Who may connect as it is then up to the permissions
accountRisk.Rotate - Description: Each account gets a new random password, set on the asset and checked by signing in with it. For an asset's own account, the asset's saved password changes too
accountRisk.Why it is fine, for the next one to read: Why it is fine, for the next one to read

accountTemplate.A preview of what applying changes, noth: A preview of what applying changes, nothing is saved yet
accountTemplate.A random password for each asset: A random password for each asset
accountTemplate.Assets - Tooltip: The assets the template gives its account to; with the asset tags, every asset with one of them too. Applying again picks up the assets added since
accountTemplate.Push - Tooltip: Set the password on the asset when the template is applied, creating the account there if it does not exist. Only on SSH assets whose own account is root, can use sudo without a password, or is a Windows administrator
accountTemplate.Random password - Tooltip: Each asset gets a random password of its own, set on the asset when the template is applied, so that one leaked password opens only one asset. It needs Push
accountTemplate.Rotate - Tooltip: Change the passwords of the accounts on a schedule, on SSH assets
accountTemplate.Saved, paste a new key to replace it: Saved, paste a new key to replace it

asset.API server - Tooltip: The address of the API server, like https://192.168.1.10:6443, with a path for a cluster behind a proxy; a host alone uses the port below
asset.Copied to the remote clipboard, press Ct: Copied to the remote clipboard, press Ctrl+V on the remote desktop to paste
asset.Copy SSH command for your public key: Copy SSH command for your public key
asset.Copy port forwarding command for your pu: Copy port forwarding command for your public key
asset.Copying files to the remote clipboard: Copying files to the remote clipboard
asset.Database - Tooltip: The database to open when connecting, can be left empty; for PostgreSQL an empty one means the database named after the user
asset.Database number - Tooltip: The Redis database to open when connecting, 0 when left empty
asset.Database of MongoDB - Tooltip: The database to open when connecting, test when left empty; the user is checked in admin first, then in this database
asset.Files copied on the remote desktop: Files copied on the remote desktop
asset.Keep it running, then connect your clien: Keep it running, then connect your client to
asset.Links and commands work once, within two: Links and commands work once, within two minutes
asset.Namespace - Tooltip: The namespace shown first, and the only one shown when the token may not list namespaces; "default" when empty
asset.Network gateway - Tooltip: Connect to the asset through an SSH jump host or an agent in its network, for assets that Casvisor cannot reach directly. A gateway in a network domain fails over to the other gateways of the domain
asset.Open in SSH client (Xshell, SecureCRT, T: Open in SSH client (Xshell, SecureCRT, Termius)
asset.Open the downloaded file to connect, wit: Open the downloaded file to connect, within two minutes
asset.Recorded on the first connection, a diff: Recorded on the first connection, a different host key or certificate is rejected afterwards. Clear it if the server was reinstalled or its certificate renewed
asset.Service name - Tooltip: The service name of the Oracle database to connect to, such as ORCLPDB1 or FREEPDB1
asset.The public key of the API server is reco: The public key of the API server is recorded on the first connection, a different one is rejected afterwards. Clear it if the cluster was reinstalled
asset.The remote computer is offline or can't: The remote computer is offline or can't be reached.
asset.The remote computer is showing the lock: The remote computer is showing the lock screen or a UAC prompt, which can't be shown here
asset.This browser can't decode the remote scr: This browser can't decode the remote screen, use a recent Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari
asset.Token - Tooltip: A bearer token of the cluster, like a service account token from "kubectl create token"; its RBAC decides which pods can be opened
asset.Username of a Kubernetes cluster - Toolt: Optional, a name for the token, which permissions and sessions show
asset.Waiting for the person at the remote com: Waiting for the person at the remote computer to allow the session...

assetImport.A CSV file or an Excel workbook whose fi: A CSV file or an Excel workbook whose first line is the header. Only the name column is required; the protocol defaults to SSH and the port to the protocol's. Nodes are paths such as Beijing/Production, separated by ";", and missing ones are created
assetImport.A CSV file whose first line is the heade: A CSV file whose first line is the header. Only the name column is required; the protocol defaults to SSH and the port to the protocol's. Nodes are paths such as Beijing/Production, separated by ";", and missing ones are created
assetImport.An existing asset keeps the values of th: An existing asset keeps the values of the columns the file leaves out, and its password and private key when those cells are empty. Exported files have no passwords, so they can be edited and imported back
assetImport.Choose a CSV or Excel file: Choose a CSV or Excel file
assetImport.The first sheet of the Excel workbook is: The first sheet of the Excel workbook is imported, with the same columns as the CSV file
assetImport.Update the assets that already exist: Update the assets that already exist

assetNode.A node name can not contain \"/\": A node name can not contain "/"
assetNode.Add to these nodes, keeping the current: Add to these nodes, keeping the current ones
assetNode.Group the assets into nodes, such as dat: Group the assets into nodes, such as data centers, environments or teams, and grant access to a whole node
assetNode.Nodes - Tooltip: The folders of the asset tree the asset is in. A permission on a node covers the assets in it and in all nodes below it
assetNode.Only a node without child nodes, assets: Only a node without child nodes, assets and permissions can be deleted
assetNode.Such as Beijing, Production or Databases: Such as Beijing, Production or Databases
assetNode.With no node chosen, the assets are take: With no node chosen, the assets are taken out of all nodes

cloudAccount.A preview of what the sync changes, noth: A preview of what the sync changes, nothing is saved yet
cloudAccount.AWS - Tooltip: An access key of an IAM user with the AmazonEC2ReadOnlyAccess policy is enough, Casvisor only lists the servers
cloudAccount.Address - Tooltip: The IP that new and synced assets are reached at. Use the private IP when Casvisor, or the network gateway below, is in the same network as the servers
cloudAccount.Aliyun - Tooltip: An AccessKey of a RAM user with the AliyunECSReadOnlyAccess policy is enough, Casvisor only lists the servers
cloudAccount.Asset tree node - Tooltip: New assets go under this node of the asset tree, in a node per region, which are created when missing. New assets go in no node when empty
cloudAccount.Azure - Tooltip: A service principal (an app registration with a client secret) with the Reader role on the subscription is enough, Casvisor only lists the virtual machines
cloudAccount.Delete missing assets - Tooltip: Delete the assets whose servers are no longer in the account. When off, they are only reported as missing. An empty list of servers never deletes anything
cloudAccount.GCP - Tooltip: The JSON key of a service account with the Compute Viewer role on the project, Casvisor only lists the instances
cloudAccount.Huawei - Tooltip: An AK/SK of an IAM user with the ECS ReadOnlyAccess policy is enough, Casvisor only lists the projects and the servers
cloudAccount.Private IP first: Private IP, or the public one when there is none
cloudAccount.Public IP first: Public IP, or the private one when there is none
cloudAccount.Regions - Tooltip: Only the servers in these regions are synced, all regions when empty. Load regions lists the regions of the account and also tells whether the credentials work
cloudAccount.Saved, paste a new key to replace it: Saved, paste a new key to replace it
cloudAccount.Sync interval - Tooltip: In minutes, at least 5. 0 syncs only when Sync is clicked
cloudAccount.Synced from - Tooltip: The cloud account this asset is synced from, and the ID of its server there. A sync updates its display name, address, OS and description
cloudAccount.Tencent - Tooltip: An API key of a CAM user with the QcloudCVMReadOnlyAccess policy is enough, Casvisor only lists the servers
cloudAccount.The project of the key when empty: The project of the key when empty
cloudAccount.The sync is done, this is what changed: The sync is done, this is what changed
cloudAccount.Usernames - Tooltip: The username new assets connect as, by the OS of the server: Linux servers become SSH assets, Windows servers RDP assets. Passwords and keys are set on the assets or their system accounts afterwards

command.Alert - Tooltip: The command runs, and is recorded with the rule and sent to the webhooks
command.Block - Tooltip: The command is not run, and the user sees the rule that blocked it
command.In database sessions the pattern is matc: In database sessions the pattern is matched against each SQL statement, SQL Server batch, Redis command or MongoDB call, for example
command.Pattern - Tooltip: A regular expression, matched anywhere in the command, for example ^\s*rm\s+-rf\s+/\s*$; in database sessions it is matched against each SQL statement
command.Review - Tooltip: The command waits until an administrator approves it on the Command reviews page, for up to 10 minutes; the user can withdraw it with Ctrl+C
command.Reviewers - Tooltip: The administrators who may approve or reject the commands this rule holds; when empty, every administrator of the organization. Nobody can review a command of their own
command.The command runs as soon as it is approv: The command runs as soon as it is approved

connectRule.Accounts - Tooltip: The system accounts of the assets the rule covers, such as root; every account when empty, and * for every account
connectRule.Methods - Tooltip: Browser is the web terminal, the remote desktop, the database console, websites and the file panel. SSH client is a terminal through the SSH gateway, such as ssh, Xshell or VS Code Remote. SFTP client covers sftp, WinSCP, scp and rsync through the gateway. Port forwarding is ssh -L through the gateway. Remote Desktop Connection is mstsc through the Remote Desktop Gateway. Every method when empty
connectRule.Priority - Tooltip: Rules are tried from the smallest priority up, and the first one that matches decides; when none matches, the connection goes on as far as the permissions allow. Put an Allow rule before a wider Reject rule to make an exception

database.No statements were run in this session: No statements were run in this session
database.Only the first {{count}} rows are shown: Only the first {{count}} rows are shown
database.Type MongoDB shell commands here, such a: Type MongoDB shell commands here, such as db.users.find({}), Ctrl+Enter runs the selected text or all of it
database.Type Redis commands here, one per line,: Type Redis commands here, one per line, Ctrl+Enter runs the selected text or all of it
database.Type SQL here, Ctrl+Enter runs the selec: Type SQL here, Ctrl+Enter runs the selected text or all of it
database.Type SQL here, end a PL/SQL block with a: Type SQL here, end a PL/SQL block with a line holding a slash, Ctrl+Enter runs the selected text or all of it
database.Type T-SQL here, separate the batches wi: Type T-SQL here, separate the batches with GO lines, Ctrl+Enter runs the selected text or all of it
database.Waiting for an administrator to approve: Waiting for an administrator to approve this statement (request {{id}})

general.Machines can be connected via RDP, VNC o: Machines can be connected via RDP, VNC or SSH

general.Run jobs at set times, such as backups e: Run jobs at set times, such as backups every night or checks every hour
general.Scan and install system updates on SSH a: Scan and install system updates on SSH assets

general.Sorry, the page you visited does not exi: Sorry, the page you visited does not exist.
general.Sorry, you do not have permission to acc: Sorry, you do not have permission to access this page or logged in status invalid.
general.This is a read-only demo site!: This is a read-only demo site!
general.Weak, old and reused passwords, and acco: Weak, old and reused passwords, and accounts on the assets that Casvisor does not manage
general.Who can connect to which assets: Who can connect to which assets
general.Zip files of the passwords and private k: Zip files of the passwords and private keys, encrypted, to download or to email on a schedule

job.A path ending with / is a folder, and th: A path ending with / is a folder, and the file keeps its name in it
job.An asset still running after this is sto: An asset still running after this is stopped
job.Bash runs on Linux assets, PowerShell on: Bash runs on Linux assets, PowerShell on Windows assets and on Linux assets with pwsh
job.Every SSH asset with one of these tags: Every SSH asset with one of these tags
job.How many assets run at the same time: How many assets run at the same time
job.Only SSH assets can run jobs: Only SSH assets can run jobs
job.Optional, such as Check disk space: Optional, such as Check disk space
job.Pick assets by name or by tag: Pick assets by name or by tag
job.Run again on the {{count}} assets that d: Run again on the {{count}} assets that did not succeed?
job.Runs as - Tooltip: The jobs run as the administrator who last saved the schedule: the command rules for that administrator apply, and the jobs are recorded under that name
job.Schedule - Tooltip: A cron expression of five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week, such as 0 3 * * * for 03:00 every day or */15 9-18 * * 1-5 for every 15 minutes in working hours. A run is skipped when the last job of the schedule is still running
job.The job schedule does not exist: The job schedule does not exist
job.Time zone - Tooltip: The time zone the schedule is read in, such as Asia/Shanghai; the server's when empty
job.What runs now is stopped, and the assets: What runs now is stopped, and the assets not reached yet are skipped.

kubernetes.Only running pods can be opened: Only running pods can be opened
kubernetes.Select a container to open a shell in it: Select a container to open a shell in it

login.Enter the 6-digit code from your authent: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app

login.The sign-in request is no longer valid: The sign-in request is no longer valid
login.Waiting for an administrator to approve: Waiting for an administrator to approve this sign-in

loginRule.Allow - Tooltip: Let the sign-in go on. Put an Allow rule before a broader Reject rule to make exceptions, such as the office network
loginRule.Client IPs - Tooltip: IPs or CIDRs such as 10.0.0.0/8; empty for every address
loginRule.Mfa - Tooltip: Ask for a code from an authenticator app. A user who hasn't turned it on must do so right after signing in on the web, and can't sign in through the SSH gateway until then
loginRule.Priority - Tooltip: Rules are tried from the smallest priority up, and the first rule that matches decides. Without a matching rule the sign-in goes on
loginRule.Reject - Tooltip: Refuse the sign-in. A rule that covers an administrator only through * or a group does not reject them, so that nobody can lock all administrators out
loginRule.Review - Tooltip: Hold the sign-in until an administrator approves it on the Login reviews page, 10 minutes at most. Like Reject, it does not hold an administrator through * or a group
loginRule.Reviewers - Tooltip: The administrators who may approve; empty for every administrator of the organization
loginRule.Sign-in methods - Tooltip: Web is signing in to the Casvisor website, SSH gateway is ssh, scp and SFTP through Casvisor; empty for both
loginRule.Time of day - Tooltip: Empty for the whole day. An end before the start, such as 22:00 to 06:00, goes over midnight and belongs to the day it starts on
loginRule.Time zone - Tooltip: An IANA time zone such as Asia/Shanghai; empty for the server's
loginRule.Users - Tooltip: Empty users and groups cover everyone
loginRule.Weekdays - Tooltip: The days the rule applies on; empty for every day
loginRule.With Casdoor sign-in, two-step verificat: With Casdoor sign-in, two-step verification is set in Casdoor, and this rule lets the sign-in go on

networkGateway.A computer running Casvisor Desktop conn: A computer running Casvisor Desktop connects out to Casvisor over HTTPS, a Desktop asset that uses it controls the computer
networkGateway.A token is set. It was shown only once,: A token is set. It was shown only once, generate a new one if it is lost
networkGateway.An agent in the other network connects o: An agent in the other network connects out to Casvisor over HTTPS and keeps the connection open, Casvisor reaches the assets that use the gateway through it
networkGateway.Casvisor connects to the gateway over SS: Casvisor connects to the gateway over SSH and reaches the assets that use it from there, the gateway needs AllowTcpForwarding
networkGateway.Network domain - Tooltip: Gateways with the same network domain reach the same network. An asset using any of them goes through a healthy one, and through the next one when it can't be reached. Leave it empty to use the gateway on its own
networkGateway.No token yet, generate one and start the: No token yet, generate one and start the agent with it
networkGateway.None, the gateway is used on its own: None, the gateway is used on its own
networkGateway.One network (CIDR) or IP address per lin: One network (CIDR) or IP address per line, the agent refuses to connect anywhere else. Leave it empty to allow every address
networkGateway.Priority - Tooltip: The gateways of a smaller number are tried first, those of a larger number only when they all fail
networkGateway.Recorded on the first connection, a diff: Recorded on the first connection, a different host key is rejected afterwards. Clear it if the gateway was reinstalled
networkGateway.The agent is disconnected right away and: The agent is disconnected right away and cannot connect again until a new token is generated
networkGateway.The agent using the current token is dis: The agent using the current token is disconnected and has to be started again with the new one
networkGateway.The token is shown only this once. Enter: The token is shown only this once. Enter these in the settings of Casvisor Desktop on the computer
networkGateway.The token is shown only this once. Run t: The token is shown only this once. Run the command on a machine in the other network, with the casvisor binary of the same release
networkGateway.Weight - Tooltip: How the connections are shared among the gateways of the same priority, a gateway of weight 2 gets twice as many as one of weight 1

Assets are not restarted automatically. Restart them afterwards if an update needs it.
patch.Connections to the assets drop while the: Connections to the assets drop while they restart. Each asset is scanned again once it is back.
patch.No SSH assets yet. Add the SSH asset of: No SSH assets yet. Add the SSH asset of a machine to manage its updates.
patch.Nothing has run on this asset yet: Nothing has run on this asset yet

permission.Accounts - Tooltip: Which accounts of the assets the users may connect as: the asset's own account, the account named like the user, all accounts, or accounts by username
permission.Nodes - Tooltip: Assets in these nodes of the asset tree and in all nodes below them, including assets added to them later
permission.The account named like the user: The account named like the user
permission.Time of day - Tooltip: Hours of the day the permission applies in, empty for the whole day. An end before the start, such as 22:00 to 06:00, goes over midnight
permission.Watermark - Tooltip: Show the user, client IP and time over the browser sessions the permission covers. A permission with no actions and the watermark on only adds the watermark to what other permissions grant, so one covering all users and all assets watermarks every session, administrators included
permission.Weekdays - Tooltip: Days of the week the permission applies on, empty for every day; sessions are disconnected when the window ends

report.Only the first 200 rows are listed: Only the first 200 rows are listed
report.Period - Tooltip: The time the report covers, counted back from when it is made: last week for a report sent every Monday, last month for one sent on the 1st
report.Reports emailed as Excel workbooks on a: Reports emailed as Excel workbooks on a cron schedule, or downloaded by hand
report.Schedule - Tooltip: A crontab line in the time zone: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week
report.Sections - Tooltip: The parts of the report, each a sheet of the workbook; all of them when none is chosen
report.Send with - Tooltip: Webhooks of the Email type; the report is attached to the email as an Excel workbook
report.Time zone - Tooltip: The time zone of the schedule, the period and the working hours, such as Asia/Shanghai; the server's when empty
report.Working hours - Tooltip: Successful sign-ins outside these days and hours are counted as off-hours sign-ins

session.Share - Description: Hand the link and the code to a colleague of the organization, who signs in and joins the session to watch it or to type in it too. You are told in the session who joins and leaves, what they type is checked against the command rules and recorded under their name, and revoking the share or its end disconnects them
session.{{user}} shares the session on {{asset}}: {{user}} shares the session on {{asset}} with you, to watch it and type in it
{{user}} shares the session on {{asset}} with you, to watch it

sshKey.Add your public key below, then connect: Add your public key below, then connect with the asset name as the username
sshKey.Connecting with your own username shows: Connecting with your own username shows a menu of your SSH assets
sshKey.Paste the content of ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.p: Paste the content of ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub, or create a key with ssh-keygen -t ed25519
sshKey.The SSH gateway is not enabled, set sshG: The SSH gateway is not enabled, set sshGatewayPort in conf/app.conf to enable it

user.For a user who lost the authenticator ap: For a user who lost the authenticator app. The user signs in with the password alone and can set it up again
user.Leave empty to keep the password: Leave empty to keep the password
user.Password - Tooltip: At least 8 characters; leave it empty to keep the current password of an existing user

web.A certificate the system trusts is alway: A certificate the system trusts is always accepted. Any other one, like a self-signed certificate, is recorded by its public key on the first connection, and a different one is rejected afterwards
web.Address - Tooltip: The address of the website, like http://192.168.1.10:3000/, whose path is the page opened first; a host alone uses the port below, over https on 443 and over http on the others
web.Basic authentication - Tooltip: With the password below, sent to the website as HTTP basic authentication. Leave both empty for a website with a sign-in page of its own
web.Next button - Tooltip: For a sign-in in two steps, the CSS selector of the button between the username and the password. Empty when both are on one page
web.No requests were sent in this session: No requests were sent in this session
web.Open in - Tooltip: Reverse proxy opens the website in the user's browser on a subdomain of webAssetDomain. Casvisor's browser runs Chrome on the server of Casvisor and shows its screen in the page: it can sign in for the user with a password the user never sees, records the screen, and keeps working when the website writes its own address into its pages
web.Password field - Tooltip: The CSS selector of the password field. Casvisor fills in the password of the account the session uses, and the user never sees it
web.Sign-in account - Tooltip: The account Casvisor signs in to the website with, in the sign-in form below. Without a sign-in form, it is sent as HTTP basic authentication
web.Sign-in button - Tooltip: The CSS selector of the button that signs in. Empty to submit the form of the password field
web.Sign-in page - Tooltip: The page with the sign-in form, on the website, like /login. Empty for the address of the website
web.The website asks for files. Choose them: The website asks for files. Choose them on this computer to upload them through Casvisor
web.The website opens in a window of its own: The website opens in a window of its own, through Casvisor
web.Username field - Tooltip: The CSS selector of the username field, like #username or input[name=email]. Casvisor fills in the username of the account the session uses

webhook.Events - Tooltip: What the webhook is told of
webhook.Recipients - Tooltip: The email addresses to send to, separated by commas
webhook.SMTP password - Tooltip: The password of the SMTP username, or the app password or authorization code that mail services such as Gmail, Outlook, QQ Mail and Tencent Exmail give for clients. It is only sent over TLS
webhook.SMTP server - Tooltip: The host and port of the mail server, such as smtp.gmail.com, smtp.exmail.qq.com or smtp.office365.com. Port 465 uses TLS from the start, other ports such as 587 use STARTTLS
webhook.SMTP username - Tooltip: The account that signs in to the mail server, usually the email address. Empty for a server on the internal network that takes mail without signing in
webhook.Secret - Tooltip: Optional; when set, each request carries X-Casvisor-Signature-256: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256 of the body>
webhook.Secret DingTalk - Tooltip: The secret of the bot's signing security setting (SEC...); without it, set the bot's keyword to Casvisor
webhook.Secret Feishu - Tooltip: The secret of the bot's signature verification; leave it empty when the bot does not verify signatures
webhook.Sender - Tooltip: The From of the emails, such as Casvisor <casvisor@example.com>. Empty: the SMTP username
webhook.Type - Tooltip: JSON posts the event as JSON for your own systems; DingTalk, Feishu, WeCom and Slack post a text message to a group bot; Email sends it with your SMTP server
webhook.URL - Tooltip: The address the events are posted to; for a group bot, the webhook address shown when the bot is added to the group
webhook.access_request.reviewed: Access request approved, rejected or revoked
webhook.job_schedule.missed: Job schedule did not start a job
